subject: Planned maintenance: East US3 kernel concordance & rolling restart (customer notice)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: ops+infra@acme-ai.com, sre-team@globex.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 08:10:00 +0000
Subject: Planned maintenance: East US3 kernel concordance & rolling restart (customer notice)

Hi team —

Heads-up: we have a scheduled maintenance window for the East US3 serving pool to perform a kernel/driver concordance update and a staggered rolling restart. This is a focused change to align kernel/drivers across the host fleet and incorporate a small runtime patch that fixes rare KV-cache eviction forks observed under long-running sequences.

Planned window (UTC):
  - Start: 2027-09-09 02:00 UTC
  - End: 2027-09-09 04:00 UTC

What to expect:
  - We will perform staggered node restarts across availability domains to keep >90% capacity serving.
  - Short-lived reconnections: any single streaming connection that spans a node restart may drop; clients should reconnect. Typical interruption is <30s per affected connection.
  - No token truncation for new requests; in-flight requests redirected when possible.
  - We will run initial canaries for 30 minutes before broad rollout and hold if any regression is detected.

Mitigations we have in place:
  - Canary node verification and automatic rollback on error rates or latency regressions.
  - Auto-fallback routing to compatible model variants for customers on Dedicated capacity.
  - Prefix KV rewarm steps after node join to restore cache hit rates.
  - Pre-notice to your SRE on exact shard list and times 24 hours before the window.

Attachments: maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook), impact-matrix.csv (sample impact estimator).

Please let us know if you have any blackout windows or critical batch jobs during the window. If you can confirm whether Acme AI has long-lived streaming sessions (duration > 10 minutes) that we should pin to a canary cohort, that would help minimize pain.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: East US3 kernel concordance & rolling restart (customer notice)

On Tue, 07 Sep 2027 at 08:10 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Heads-up: we have a scheduled maintenance window for the East US3 serving pool ...

Thanks for the notice, Rishi. We appreciate the level of detail. A couple quick items from Acme AI ops: 

  1) We run a nightly batch of long-running scoring jobs that touch the streaming API; those start at ~02:15 UTC and run for ~40–60 minutes. If the maintenance coincides, we'll see a backlog that impacts downstream data pipelines.
  2) Can you confirm whether public IPs for any egress paths will change, or if any ephemeral IP rotation happens? Our firewall rules are tight.
  3) If there is customer-visible error spike, what's the process to request an SLA credit? Please point me to the support flow.

If possible we'd prefer shifting the window to start 2 hours later (04:00–06:00 UTC) to avoid the batch. If that's not feasible, we can provide a list of long-lived jobs to exclude from the canary pool.

-Ashley
Ashley King
Platform Engineer, Acme AI
ops+infra@acme-ai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ashley King <ashley.king@acme-ai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: East US3 kernel concordance & rolling restart (customer notice)

Hi Ashley —

Thanks for flagging the batch window. We can accommodate a later window and will shift the East US3 rollout to 04:00–06:00 UTC on 2027-09-09 to avoid the 02:15 job start. Plan summary: 

  - Canary nodes will run from 04:00–04:30 UTC (small shard set).
  - If canaries are green, gradual draining and restart of remaining nodes will proceed 04:30–06:00 UTC.
  - No egress IP changes during this operation; NAT/egress ranges remain stable. Any host-level IP reassignment would be handled by provider tooling and is not part of this change.
  - For SLA/credits: please open a standard support ticket and reference INC-2027-09-07; we'll expedite review if there's a customer-visible regression.

Action items for Acme AI (please reply):
  - Confirm the list of long-lived jobs (service names or job IDs) you want excluded from the canary/test cohort.
  - Any additional blackout constraints (we have buffer hours on either side if needed).

Link: runbook snapshot (maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf) attached; also attaching a short impact matrix we've used for similar regional rollouts.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ashley King <ashley.king@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Post-maintenance: East US3 kernel concordance — brief follow-up and summary

Ashley / team —

Thanks again for coordinating. We completed the East US3 kernel concordance and rolling restart on 2027-09-09 between 04:00–05:42 UTC (we finished early after canaries validated). Quick summary: 

  - Scope: kernel + driver alignment across host fleet, plus runtime patch to address KV-cache eviction corner-case.
  - Observed customer impact: ~0.03% of requests experienced a transient reconnect and resumed successfully; no requests reported token loss. Streaming sessions that overlapped a node restart required reconnect; we observed median reconnect time of 18s.
  - Rollback: none required — canaries and incremental rollout were all green.
  - Remediations and follow-ups: we added an extra KV-warm job for node join, expanded canary cohort for future rollouts, and improved our pre-rollout checklist to capture customers with scheduled batch jobs.

Attachments: postmortem-summary-20270909.md (brief), and the runbook we used (maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf). Full postmortem and telemetry are available at: https://drive.google.com/open?id=postmortem-20270907 and the internal incident: https://redwood.app/console/incident/INC-2027-09-07.

If you saw anything unexpected on your side, please reply and we'll prioritize a deep-dive. We'll also follow up with a short call if you'd like to walk through the telemetry.

Regards —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
